transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood CSM), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Spectra Health - Head of MLOps), Liam O'Connor (CTO), Sofia Reyes (Security), Ethan Brooks (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on onboarding plan for Spectra Health onboarding to Redwood Dedicated / Private options. Confirm security needs (SOC2, KMS), SSO, timeline for pilot, and initial perf benchmarks. Agree on next steps and owners.

Topics:
- Onboarding timeline and milestones
- Security and compliance (SOC2, SAML/SSO, audit logs, KMS)
- Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC
- Initial benchmark scope and dataset access
- Rollout plan and success criteria

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate it. Um, quick roundtable — I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE, Priya's with me, and Daniel our SE. How, uh, how's everyone doing?
[00:10] Maya: Good, thanks. Excited to get this started. We're looking to onboard Redwood for inference across a couple microservices.
[00:20] Liam: Hi, Liam here — CTO. Goal is to reduce latency for our clinical search and keep PHI controls tight.
[00:30] Priya: Awesome. So today we want to align on timeline, security checklist, and the perf tests we'll run. Daniel, feel free to jump in with the tech bits.
[00:40] Daniel: Yep. Quick note — we typically recommend starting with Dedicated for predictable throughput then evaluate Private/VPC if you need on-prem or stricter network controls. But depends on their compliance needs.
[00:50] Sofia: On the compliance side, SOC 2 is table stakes, also need to confirm audit log retention and KMS integration. We use a customer-managed key for encryption at rest.
[01:05] Jordan: Totally, we support KMS/HSM integrations on Private and Dedicated, and audit logs are available; retention is configurable. We'll share the security pack after this call.
[01:20] Ethan: Quick Q — does Dedicated give us VPC peering or do we need Private for that? We run in AWS and want minimal network hops.
[01:30] Daniel: Dedicated can do private connectivity options and peering; Private gives you a private control plane inside your VPC. If you need full air-gapped on-prem, that's Private on-prem. There's often some confusion there — sorry for the jargon.
[01:45] Maya: For our first pilot, we want dedicated GPU capacity in us-east-1, low 99p latency under 150ms for our typical 256-token requests. Latency vs cost tradeoff is a concern though.
[02:00] Jordan: Good — that gives a clear target. We'll recommend a model variant and quantization profile to hit that latency while keeping cost manageable. Our Redwood Optimize tool will help with batching and cache suggestions.
[02:15] Liam: We'll need SSO: SAML with SCIM provisioning, and RBAC so product teams get narrow permissions.
[02:25] Priya: We have SSO docs and SCIM flows; I'll send the SAML metadata and a short setup guide.
[02:35] Sofia: Also, do you have penetration test reports and your SOC 2 cert? Need those for procurement.
[02:45] Jordan: Yes, we'll attach the SOC2 Type II and pen test summary in the security packet.
[02:55] Ethan: On the bench — what does the perf test look like? We want realistic load: mix of 80% short prompts, 20% 512-token long.
[03:05] Daniel: For perf we usually run an internal perf harness with a replay of 10k requests across your distribution. We'll also do KV cache warmup and prefix caching to mimic production. We'll coordinate on a dataset subset; ideally you provide anonymized examples.
[03:20] Maya: We can share a redacted dataset and a sample traffic distribution next week.
[03:25] Daniel: Perfect. Also need to confirm if you want continuous batching enabled at the gateway or per-instance. That will affect latency profiles.
[03:35] Jordan: Implementation plan — week 1: SSO, initial config, staging access; week 2: perf bench and metrics; week 3: pilot rollout internal. Is that feasible?
[03:45] Liam: That timeline looks fine but procurement needs the security docs before legal signs off.
[03:55] Jordan: Understood. We'll prioritize sending the security packet today.
[04:05] Priya: I'll also set up bi-weekly check-ins and a Slack channel for faster comms.
[04:15] Maya: Great. A couple of risk notes: data residency — some records must stay in us-east-1 only. Also, we may need to support redaction of PHI before sending to Redwood, is there guidance?
[04:30] Daniel: We have a few options: client-side redaction, or use Private deployment with in-network preprocessing. We can help architect that.
[04:40] Sofia: And logging — we need a way to ensure PHI doesn't land in logs. Can logs be scrubbed or stored in your KMS-protected buckets?
[04:55] Jordan: Yes, log scrubbing options exist and we can ensure logs are stored in customer-controlled buckets with CMEK. We'll include config examples.
[05:05] Ethan: On costs — are there burst credits if we need to handle spikes?
[05:15] Jordan: Dedicated has burst capacity options; we can outline pricing tiers. For the pilot we can recommend a small reserved pool and enable burst to avoid throttling.
[05:25] Priya: I'll send a pilot pricing spreadsheet with projected monthly token estimates and cost ranges.
[05:35] Maya: Sounds good. For the pilot success criteria — low latency for 95th/99th, <0.1% error rate, and no data leakage events.
[05:45] Daniel: We'll instrument trace ids and give per-route dashboards in Redwood Console for token-level cost, latency breakdowns, and error analysis.
[05:55] Jordan: Great. Any blockers we should note?
[06:00] Liam: Procurement will want the SOC 2, contract terms, and data processing agreement. Also need clarity on support SLAs.
[06:10] Jordan: We'll include SLA tiers and support options in the packet. For enterprise Private deployments we offer premium SLAs.
[06:20] Maya: Okay, if you can send the security packet and onboarding deck today, we'll review and come back with a date for the perf dataset share.
[06:30] Priya: I'll set up the calendar invite for the technical walkthrough next week and include Daniel.
[06:40] Ethan: Quick nit — what's the recommended model? We're leaning open weights, any Redwood recommendations?
[06:50] Daniel: For inference cost/latency tradeoffs we'd probably recommend a quantized optimized open model from our catalog; we'll propose a specific variant after seeing your latency goal and quality requirements. If you need higher quality we can suggest a larger model but that affects latency/cost.
[07:05] Maya: Good. Please include the model recommendations and quantization impacts in the follow-up.
[07:15] Jordan: Recap of next steps: Jordan send security and onboarding docs; Priya send checklist & pricing sheet; Daniel schedule technical walkthrough and perf plan; Maya share dataset ETA and stakeholders.
[07:30] Liam: Thanks all. Look forward to the packet.
[07:35] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and post the links to the shared folder. Bye.

End of transcript.
